source.authors: Wojciech Paszta, Karolina Goździewska-Harłajczuk, Joanna Klećkowska-Nawrot
source.title: Morphology and Histology of the Orbital Region and Eye of the Asiatic Black Bear (Ursus thibetanus)—Similarities and Differences within the Caniformia Suborder

method: gross eyeball morphometry and histology (Fontana-Masson, H&E, Movat and other stains) of the eye tunics
conditions: One captive adult male Asiatic black bear (27 years 4 months 10 days) from Wroclaw Zoological Garden, Poland, euthanised for a non-healing jaw wound; material taken post mortem. The paper lists eyeballs as n = 2 in one section but the material is one animal; six random caliper measurements per structure were recorded as mean +/- SD, with morphometry done before fixation in 4% buffered formaldehyde. Not a species mean (n = 1 animal). The Results describe the structure as very faintly marked, a slightly opalescent dark-brown crescent (8.063 +/- 0.05 mm long), and as a choroidal tapetum lucidum cellulosum of loosely packed degenerate cells in 2-3 layers; those sentences are not quoted.
quote: Degenerative choroidal tapetum lucidum similar to ranch mink (Mustelidae) has been found.
note: Whole Abstract sentence (12 words), read in a second pass of the abstract (sentence 6 of 17). Value follows the sentence; 'similar to ranch mink' is a comparison made by the authors, not a measurement. New species for tapetum on main (no Ursus thibetanus or this DOI anywhere in docs/ or desk-d23*/d24* evidence). Licence: the page prints no licence sentence in the text read; its metadata links CC BY 3.0, and Crossref lists CC BY 4.0 with content-version vor (accepted pairing). Crossref spells the second author Gożdziewska-Harłajczuk; the page spelling Goździewska-Harłajczuk is used. Crossref authors (3), volume 12, issue 7, year 2022 agree. Family Ursidae and order Carnivora as filed on main for Ursus (canon-3 row); the name Ursus thibetanus is not in gbif-names.tsv (no SYNONYM row); WoRMS/OBIS not applicable.

source.title: Morphology and Histology of the Orbital Region and Eye of the Asiatic Black Bear (Ursus thibetanus)—Similarities and Differences within the Caniformia Suborder

method: digital caliper on the whole eyeball, six random measurements, mean +/- SD (0.4 mm), before fixation; value given as 'approximately'
conditions: One captive adult male Asiatic black bear (27 years 4 months 10 days) from Wroclaw Zoological Garden, Poland, euthanised for a non-healing jaw wound; material taken post mortem. The paper lists eyeballs as n = 2 in one section but the material is one animal; six random caliper measurements per structure were recorded as mean +/- SD, with morphometry done before fixation in 4% buffered formaldehyde. Not a species mean (n = 1 animal). The paper's other eyeball figures disagree internally: the maximum transverse diameter is printed as 17.127 +/- 0.09 mm and the minimum transverse diameter as 18.143 +/- 0.08 mm (minimum larger than maximum), so the printed morphometry may contain an error; the Abstract gives no diameters. 'Axial eye diameter' is read as the axial length (owner question).
quote: The axial eye diameter was 16.7 ± 0.4 mm, approximately.
note: Whole Results sentence (10 words) read intact in two passes. New trait for this species: eye_axial_length_mm is a key already on main (absent from the checker list). Value is the printed mean; SD 0.4 mm over six caliper repeats on one animal's eyeball, not a between-animal spread. No Ursus thibetanus or this DOI elsewhere in docs/ or desk-d23*/d24* evidence. source.authors: Amira Derbalah, Samir A. A. El-Gendy, Hanan H. Abd-Elhafeez, Soha Soliman, Ahmed A. El-Mansi, Manal Seif, Ahmed M. Rashwan, Mamdouh B. Eldesoqui, Catrin Sian Rutland, Valentina Kubale, Mohamed A. M. Alsafy
source.title: Light and scanning electron microscopy of the eye of Siganus luridus (Rüppell, 1828)

method: eye-shine under a flashing light on freshly collected eyes, plus light and scanning electron microscopy; the Results text (section 3.1) reads the eye-shine as indicating a tapetum lucidum and section 3.4 describes it as dense choroidal tissue infiltrated with melanocytes and blood vessels
conditions: Ten mature, healthy fish 'collected from the Mediterranean Sea (Damietta Governorate)' (the paper does not say wild-caught or bought at a market, how they were killed, or the time from capture to examination); mean body length 16.20 +/- 1.21 cm; eyes were 'freshly collected'. The paper gives no eye count per method. Presence only: no reflectance, thickness or eye-shine spectrum is reported. The authors note it is unexpected because herbivores typically lack a tapetum.
quote: The tapetum lucidum was observed, which is interesting since Siganus luridus is herbivore and herbivores typically lack a tapetum lucidum.
note: Whole Abstract sentence (21 words), read in two abutting pieces (14th and 15th lines of the abstract, second pass; the sentence before ends 'in the choroidal gland'). New species for tapetum on main (Siganus luridus appears only in docs/views/gaps/try-species.json; this DOI nowhere). Family and order as filed on main for Siganidae (Perciformes); species name is the accepted one in the paper's title (OBIS/WoRMS page could not be opened). Licence: the page prints no licence sentence; Crossref lists CC BY 4.0, content-version vor (accepted). Crossref authors (11, listed here), volume 11, year 2024 agree; the page lists a different author count display ('+2 more') and prints no issue number.
